# Founder Brain

- **Founder:** Sam Okoye
- **Business:** Northfield Ops
- **Track:** b2b
- **Hybrid:** false
- **Stage:** First customers, roughly 6k GBP per month
- **Locked:** 2026-08-19

## Thesis

I take the admin off owner-managed construction firms turning over 1M to 5M, so the owner stops doing job costing at 10pm. I do it as someone who ran sites for fifteen years, not as a consultant who has read about it.

## Offer

Fractional operations support for construction SMEs turning over 1M to 5M. Sam takes over scheduling, subcontractor coordination and job costing for firms where the owner is still running it all from a phone and a whiteboard.

Priced as a monthly retainer, 1,800 to 3,200 GBP depending on job volume. Three-month minimum, then rolling.

The problem in customer language: "I'm on site all day and doing the admin at 10pm, and I've stopped bidding on work because I can't cope with what I've already won."

Why Sam: fifteen years as a site manager before this, so he understands the trade rather than arriving as a generic consultant. Owners stop explaining the basics to him in the first ten minutes.

## Audience

**Firmographics.** Construction and building services SMEs. 1M to 5M turnover. 8 to 40 staff. UK, concentrated in the Midlands and North West. Owner-managed rather than PE-backed or family-board.

**Buyer.** The owner or managing director. Almost never a delegated decision. They sign, they onboard, they are the bottleneck being solved.

**Trigger events.** Winning a contract materially larger than their usual. Losing an office manager. A failed audit or a costing mistake that ate the margin on a job. Taking on their first project manager and realising nothing is documented.

**Three best-fit accounts today.** Halewood Building Services, Trentham Mechanical, Castlefield Contracts.

## Proof

- Trentham Mechanical: cut invoice-to-payment from 71 days to 38 in four months.
- Halewood: rebuilt job costing, found 4% margin leakage on two live projects.
- Two testimonials on file, both from owners, both naming the 10pm admin problem.
- Fifteen years on site before consulting.

Proof is decent on outcome, thin on volume. Two named cases is enough to write from, not enough to lead every post with. Content should lean on the operational detail Sam knows, not on case study volume he does not have.

## Goal, next 90 days

Three new retainers. That is roughly 7k GBP per month added, which takes him past the point of needing to take site work to fill gaps.

- **Active:** LinkedIn, posts sporadically, roughly twice a month. 1,400 connections, mostly genuine industry.
- **Dormant:** X account, unused since 2023.
- **Email:** northfieldops.co.uk on Google Workspace, with real sending history from client correspondence. No fresh domain needed, and Apollo can send from it.

**Destinations.** Website northfieldops.co.uk, one page, dated. No booking link yet, so calls get arranged by email back and forth. Sender name on email is Sam Okoye, phone 07700 900412. Setting up a booking link is the first thing his ops workflow should fix.

**Baselines, today.** LinkedIn 1,400 connections. No email list. No CRM. Roughly two inbound enquiries a month, both by word of mouth.

## Source material

Topics only, not voice. What Sam's buyers are already reading and arguing about.

- Construction News and Building magazine, for the contract awards and insolvency stories owners actually talk about.
- The Construction Index, for tender and pipeline news in the Midlands and North West.
- Two LinkedIn accounts posting weekly on subcontractor payment terms and retentions.
- A fractional operations newsletter aimed at owner-managed firms, which Sam disagrees with roughly half the time. Useful for that reason.
- The Federation of Master Builders and Build UK output on late payment and cash flow.
- Two competing fractional ops consultancies, watched for what they claim and what they charge. Topics only. Never voice.
- Reddit r/ConstructionUK, for the unfiltered version of the 10pm admin problem.

## Voice

Writes the way he talks on site. Short sentences. Plain, concrete, no consultant register. Names the specific thing rather than the category, so "the whiteboard in the portacabin" rather than "manual processes". Slightly dry, occasionally blunt, never salesy. Uses "look" and "the truth is" as openers. Rarely asks rhetorical questions and does not use lists.

Verbatim phrases: "the whiteboard in the portacabin", "you're not disorganised, you're overloaded", "nobody's got a system, they've got a memory", "that'll cost you on the next job".

## Flags

- Proof is thin on volume. Two named cases only.
- Has never run outreach. No list, no sequence, no CRM.
- LinkedIn presence exists but is inconsistent, so the content engine has a real audience to switch on rather than one to build from zero.
- Domain is established. No warmup needed.
